species.structure: oleic anhydride, the precursor (fuel) dissolved in the nitrobenzene oil phase
oleate, the surfactant anion that lowers interfacial tension
proton released at the interface; it is the local drop in pH that raises the tension and drives the Marangoni flow
the oil solvent; it carries the precursor and does not react

interaction_law.name: Marangoni flow driven by interfacial hydrolysis (onboard fuel)
interaction_law.configuration: onboard fuel: the droplet carries its own precursor and moves for minutes to hours, until the fuel runs out or waste accumulates
steps: oleic anhydride meets water at the oil-water interface and hydrolyses to two oleic acids, which deprotonate to oleate and protons
the reaction is not even over the surface, so the local pH is not even
interfacial tension rises as local pH falls (maximum at pH 9), so the tension is not even either

the tension gradient is a Marangoni force tangential to the surface, which drives Marangoni flow; once the initial symmetry breaks by fluctuation a pair of convective vortices organises inside the droplet
the convective flow brings fresh precursor to one pole and releases product at the other, which sustains the imbalance instead of equilibrating it
the droplet moves along the axis of the convection, leaving a low-pH trail of expelled surfactant behind it
interaction_law.motor: the convective flow structure inside the droplet

chemotaxis.stimulus: pH gradient, self-generated or externally imposed
chemotaxis.direction: up the gradient, toward the highest pH
chemotaxis.source: Banzhaf & Yamamoto (2015) section 19.2.5; Hanczyc & Ikegami (2010) section 3.1

tension.source: Hanczyc & Ikegami, Artificial Life 16(3):233-243 (2010), figure 2 and section 3.1; pendant-drop tensiometry, each point in triplicate
tension.relation: interfacial tension increases as pH decreases from the bulk pH 11, reaching a maximum at pH 9; at pH 11 the tension is already low, so producing more oleate has little further effect and it is the local drop in pH, not the extra surfactant, that moves the droplet

analysis.why_no_trajectory: the propulsion mechanism is published qualitatively (a Marangoni force set by the interfacial-tension gradient) but no accessible source gives the force law or a droplet speed, so Chemart records the mechanism and the measured behaviour instead of integrating a trajectory

tension.source: Hanczyc & Ikegami, Artificial Life 16(3):233-243 (2010), figure 2 and section 3.1; pendant-drop tensiometry, each point in triplicate
tension.relation: interfacial tension increases as pH decreases from the bulk pH 11, reaching a maximum at pH 9; at pH 11 the tension is already low, so producing more oleate has little further effect and it is the local drop in pH, not the extra surfactant, that moves the droplet

analysis.overall_reaction: oleic_anhydride + H2O -> 2 oleate + 2 H (hydrolysis followed by deprotonation of both oleic acids)

measured_behaviour.source: Horibe, Hanczyc & Ikegami, Entropy 13(3):709-719 (2011), doi:10.3390/e13030709 (open access)
measured_behaviour.oil: fresh oleic anhydride mixed with nitrobenzene at 1:1 v/v
findings: velocity falls and turning angle rises as the droplet ages
turning angle is negatively correlated with velocity: droplets change direction while stopped
the reaction happens at the surface, so the reaction rate is set by droplet size, and it weakens as the oil volume is consumed
spontaneous (non-collision) events give a coefficient of restitution with mean around 1, and values above 1 when the reaction is re-activated
two droplets of 3 or 20 uL stay closer together than two droplets in separate dishes, and the attraction weakens over time; 50 uL droplets, whose convective flow is unstable, show no attraction

sizes_and_timings.oil: oleic anhydride in nitrobenzene at 0.5 M (appendix A.2)
sizes_and_timings.aqueous: oleate micelles at pH 11, NaOH-adjusted (appendix A.1)
sizes_and_timings.diameter_range: a few hundred microns to a few centimetres
sizes_and_timings.onset: the droplet starts moving within seconds of the oil meeting the water
sizes_and_timings.without_precursor: droplets still move chemotactically in a pH gradient, but the motion is not sustained and stops within a few seconds once the tension imbalance is equilibrated
sizes_and_timings.mechanism_shift: above a few hundred microns self-movement shifts from convection-driven to shape-driven, and a horseshoe shape best supports straight directional motion
